final_answer:
The performance of ablated versions of LightRAG is evaluated using NaiveRAG as a reference and is detailed in Table 2 [1]. The ablation studies focus on analyzing the impact of the dual-level retrieval paradigm and the effectiveness of graph-based text indexing in LightRAG [2].

### Main Findings
1. **Low-level-only Retrieval (LightRAG -High)**: Removing high-order retrieval leads to a significant performance decline across nearly all datasets and metrics. This variant emphasizes specific information and entities, which can limit its ability to address complex queries requiring comprehensive insights [6].
2. **High-level-only Retrieval (LightRAG -Low)**: This variant prioritizes broader content by leveraging entity-wise relationships. While it excels in comprehensiveness, it sacrifices depth in examining specific entities, which can limit its ability to provide highly detailed insights [6].
3. **Hybrid Mode (Full LightRAG)**: Combining the strengths of both low-level and high-level retrieval methods, the hybrid mode ensures balanced performance across multiple dimensions by retrieving a broader set of relationships while conducting in-depth exploration of specific entities [6].
4. **Semantic Graph-based Indexing (LightRAG -Origin)**: Eliminating the use of original text in the retrieval process does not significantly degrade performance. In some cases, such as the Agriculture and Mix datasets, this variant even shows improvements. This is attributed to the effective extraction of key information during the graph-based indexing process [6].

### Representative Figures
- **Comprehensiveness**:
  - Agriculture: LightRAG (67.6%) vs. NaiveRAG (32.4%); LightRAG -High (65.2%) vs. NaiveRAG (34.8%); LightRAG -Low (64.0%) vs. NaiveRAG (36.0%); LightRAG -Origin (75.2%) vs. NaiveRAG (24.8%) [1].
  - CS: LightRAG (61.6%) vs. NaiveRAG (38.4%); LightRAG -High (57.2%) vs. NaiveRAG (42.8%); LightRAG -Low (56.8%) vs. NaiveRAG (43.2%); LightRAG -Origin (60.8%) vs. NaiveRAG (39.2%) [1].
  - Legal: LightRAG (83.6%) vs. NaiveRAG (16.4%); LightRAG -High (76.4%) vs. NaiveRAG (23.6%); LightRAG -Low (80.8%) vs. NaiveRAG (19.2%); LightRAG -Origin (83.6%) vs. NaiveRAG (16.4%) [1].
  - Mix: LightRAG (61.2%) vs. NaiveRAG (38.8%); LightRAG -High (59.6%) vs. NaiveRAG (40.4%); LightRAG -Low (64.0%) vs. NaiveRAG (36.0%); LightRAG -Origin (55.6%) vs. NaiveRAG (44.4%) [1].

- **Diversity**:
  - Agriculture: LightRAG (76.4%) vs. NaiveRAG (23.6%); LightRAG -High (72.8%) vs. NaiveRAG (27.2%); LightRAG -Low (72.0%) vs. NaiveRAG (28.0%); LightRAG -Origin (73.6%) vs. NaiveRAG (26.4%) [1].
  - CS: LightRAG (62.0%) vs. NaiveRAG (38.0%); LightRAG -High (63.2%) vs. NaiveRAG (36.8%); LightRAG -Low (60.4%) vs. NaiveRAG (39.6%); LightRAG -Origin (55.2%) vs. NaiveRAG (44.8%) [1].
  - Legal: LightRAG (86.4%) vs. NaiveRAG (13.6%); LightRAG -High (83.2%) vs. NaiveRAG (16.8%); LightRAG -Low (86.4%) vs. NaiveRAG (13.6%); LightRAG -Origin (85.6%) vs. NaiveRAG (14.4%) [1].
  - Mix: LightRAG (67.6%) vs. NaiveRAG (32.4%); LightRAG -High (64.0%) vs. NaiveRAG (36.0%); LightRAG -Low (66.8%) vs. NaiveRAG (33.2%); LightRAG -Origin (74.4%) vs. NaiveRAG (25.6%) [1].

- **Empowerment**:
  - Agriculture: LightRAG (67.6%) vs. NaiveRAG (32.4%); LightRAG -High (64.0%) vs. NaiveRAG (36.0%); LightRAG -Low (65.2%) vs. NaiveRAG (34.8%); LightRAG -Origin (68.0%) vs. NaiveRAG (32.0%) [1].
  - CS: LightRAG (61.2%) vs. NaiveRAG (38.8%); LightRAG -High (57.6%) vs. NaiveRAG (42.4%); LightRAG -Low (57.2%) vs. NaiveRAG (42.8%); LightRAG -Origin (56.8%) vs. NaiveRAG (43.2%) [1].
  - Legal: LightRAG (83.6%) vs. NaiveRAG (16.4%); LightRAG -High (77.2%) vs. NaiveRAG (22.8%); LightRAG -Low (83.6%) vs. NaiveRAG (16.4%); LightRAG -Origin (82.8%) vs. NaiveRAG (17.2%) [1].
  - Mix: LightRAG (57.2%) vs. NaiveRAG (42.8%); LightRAG -High (52.4%) vs. NaiveRAG (47.6%); LightRAG -Low (64.8%) vs. NaiveRAG (35.2%); LightRAG -Origin (54.8%) vs. NaiveRAG (45.2%) [1].

- **Overall**:
  - Agriculture: LightRAG (67.6%) vs. NaiveRAG (32.4%); LightRAG -High (64.8%) vs. NaiveRAG (35.2%); LightRAG -Low (65.2%) vs. NaiveRAG (34.8%); LightRAG -Origin (74.4%) vs. NaiveRAG (25.6%) [1].
  - CS: LightRAG (61.2%) vs. NaiveRAG (38.8%); LightRAG -High (56.0%) vs. NaiveRAG (44.0%); LightRAG -Low (56.4%) vs. NaiveRAG (43.6%); LightRAG -Origin (60.8%) vs. NaiveRAG (39.2%) [1].
  - Legal: LightRAG (84.8%) vs. NaiveRAG (15.2%); LightRAG -High (78.0%) vs. NaiveRAG (22.0%); LightRAG -Low (81.2%) vs. NaiveRAG (18.8%); LightRAG -Origin (84.4%) vs. NaiveRAG (15.6%) [1].
  - Mix: LightRAG (60.0%) vs. NaiveRAG (40.0%); LightRAG -High (57.6%) vs. NaiveRAG (42.4%); LightRAG -Low (64.8%) vs. NaiveRAG (35.2%); LightRAG -Origin (55.6%) vs. NaiveRAG (44.4%) [1].

### Results That Go Against the Trend
- **LightRAG -Low in Mix for Empowerment**: LightRAG -Low (64.8%) outperforms NaiveRAG (35.2%), which aligns with the general trend, but the performance gain is notable compared to its lower performance in other metrics [1].
- **LightRAG -Origin in Mix for Overall**: LightRAG -Origin (55.6%) outperforms NaiveRAG (44.4%), showing an improvement in this case [1].

### Conclusion
The ablation studies demonstrate that the full LightRAG model, which combines both low-level and high-level retrieval methods, achieves balanced performance across multiple dimensions. Variants that remove either retrieval level (LightRAG -High or LightRAG -Low) show performance declines in certain metrics, while the semantic graph-based indexing variant (LightRAG -Origin) maintains or even improves performance in some cases. These findings highlight the importance of the dual-level retrieval paradigm and the effectiveness of graph-based text indexing in LightRAG.
